messages:
Maya (platform): Heads-up — we have a small late-hour telemetry window (2h) for eu-prod that needs a targeted replay. low-risk but will touch agg-hours. thinking operator override + temporary shard-level quota shim. want to run a dry-run preflight in console first.
Jon (ops): ok. estimated tokens ~120M, cost ~ $12k if full run. can we micro-canary 2 shards first? :thinking_face:
Lee (eng-runtime): micro-canary SGTM. note: we should warm the KV cache for those shards or first-token latency spikes will kill the SLOs. I can add a KV-warmup step to the job if we flag it as canary.
Sasha (console): for the console UX: we can add a one-off "preflight dry-run" checkbox that simulates routing/quota effects and shows estimated cost + per-route slot usage. want to avoid baking a new API for this. question: should preflight mutate a temporary quota-shim resource or simulate only?
Maya (platform): prefer simulate-only in preflight, then separate operator action to apply real shim. keep the operator workflow explicit.
Jon (ops): operator step should be small: label tenant with "op:latehour-shim=5179" and set shard_quota=+4 for 3h. ops runbook snippet:
```
# apply shim
redwoodctl tenants patch acme-prod --labels op:latehour-shim=5179 --set shards.quota_delta=4 --duration 3h
# run canary
redwoodctl backfill start --shards 2 --cohort canary --dry-run=false --tag latehour-5179
```
Lee (eng-runtime): perfect. also recommend adding --kv-warmup=true to the backfill job so the runtime primes caches before user traffic hits it. can we default canary to 1.5x cpu?
Sasha (console): console can show the proposed resource bump and a diff view. I can wire the dry-run button to call /api/v1/preflight/backfill which will return simulated slot allocation and cost. we need API debate: lightweight read-only endpoint vs reusing existing planner.
Maya (platform): prefer new read-only preflight endpoint to avoid entangling planner state. keep it idempotent and auth-guarded for operators only.
Jon (ops): small security note — ensure preflight responses redact PII and internal tenant ids. also need telemetry metrics emitted: preflight.id and estimated_cost_usd so finance can ingest.
backfill-bot: scheduled job created: backfill-preflight:latehour-5179 (canary shards=2) — status: queued
Lee (eng-runtime): quick perf note: canary should run with kv-warmup and cache TTL set to 15m for the job to avoid long lived cache churn. I'll add a small change to the runtime config.
Sasha (console): I'll prototype the dry-run UI in the console prototype channel and post screenshots by EOD.
Maya (platform): action items: 1) Lee add kv-warmup flag + default for canary 2) Jon update ops runbook with label command 3) Sasha implement preflight dry-run UI + call to read-only /preflight API 4) Maya create the preflight API ticket and spec (auth + telemetry fields). Anyone want to own the API ticket?
Jon (ops): I can own the ticket, will spec telemetry fields with finance.
Lee (eng-runtime): I'll open a tiny PR for kv-warmup flag, link to ticket.
Sasha (console): I'll add console prototype and API contract in the ticket comments.
Maya (platform): sweet. If all thumbs-up we'll do canary at 23:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
Jon (ops): +1
Lee (eng-runtime): +1
Sasha (console): +1
Maya (platform): thanks — tagging @oncall in case something slips: @oncall please watch the canary window 23:00-01:00 UTC, ops will have rollback knobs and we'll auto-fallback to last-good aggregates on error.
backfill-bot: note: fallback policy configured: on >5% regression revert to last-good model/state and abort remaining shards.
Maya (platform): OK closing thread — will post final preflight link when API ticket lands.
